name: Suricata Rule Syntax — Anatomy, Content Modifiers & PCRE
command: alert http $HOME_NET any -> $EXTERNAL_NET any (msg:"Rule description"; content:"pattern"; sid:1000001; rev:1;)
description: Complete Suricata rule structure: header (action + protocol + IP/port + direction) and body (msg, content, flow, dsize, detection_filter, PCRE, buffers, modifiers). Actions: alert/log/pass/drop/reject. Protocols: tcp/udp/icmp/ip/http/tls/smb/dns. Content modifiers: nocase/offset/depth/distance/within. Rule buffers enable scoped inspection. PCRE provides regex matching. detection_filter adds threshold-based alerting.
notes:
=== RULE STRUCTURE ===
Full format:
  action proto src_ip src_port -> dst_ip dst_port (options)

Example:
  alert http $HOME_NET any -> $EXTERNAL_NET any (msg:"ET MALWARE..."; content:"pattern"; sid:10000001; rev:1;)

=== HEADER FIELDS ===
[ACTION]
  alert  → generate alert
  log    → log without alerting
  pass   → allow/ignore (whitelist)
  drop   → drop packet (IPS mode)
  reject → send TCP RST / ICMP unreachable, then drop

[PROTOCOL]
  tcp, udp, icmp, ip        → layer 4
  http, tls, smb, dns       → application layer (Suricata decodes)

[IP/PORT SPECIFICATION]
  $HOME_NET any -> $EXTERNAL_NET 9090   → outbound on port 9090
  $EXTERNAL_NET any -> $HOME_NET 8443   → inbound on port 8443
  $EXTERNAL_NET any <> $HOME_NET any    → bidirectional
  [8443,8080,7001:7002,!8443]           → port list with range and exclusion
  $UNCOMMON_PORTS                        → defined in suricata.yaml

=== RULE OPTIONS ===
[MSG] — alert message:
  msg:"ET MALWARE Dridex Infection";
  → Should include: malware family, action, version/variant

[FLOW] — track session direction:
  flow:established,to_server;    → client→server in existing TCP session
  flow:established,from_server;  → server→client
  flow:to_server;                → new or established, toward server
  flow:from_client;              → UDP, from originating side
  → BEST PRACTICE: always add flow:established for TCP rules

[CONTENT] — byte pattern matching:
  content:"User-Agent: Go-http-client/1.1";
  content:"|3a 20|";               → hex bytes (3a=colon, 20=space)
  content:"|0d 0a|";               → \r\n (CRLF, end of HTTP header line)
  Multiple content: keywords allowed per rule (all must match)

[CONTENT MODIFIERS — position]:
  offset:0     → start matching from byte 0 of payload
  depth:5      → only match within first 5 bytes (from offset)
  distance:10  → next content must start ≥10 bytes after previous match end
  within:80    → next content must match within 80 bytes of previous match end
  → offset+depth: absolute window; distance+within: relative window

[CONTENT MODIFIERS — other]:
  nocase            → case-insensitive match
  fast_pattern      → hint to use this content for fast pre-filter

[RULE BUFFERS] — scope matching to protocol fields:
  http_method        → match in HTTP method field only
  http_uri           → match in HTTP URI only
  http_cookie        → match in HTTP Cookie header only
  http_user_agent    → match in User-Agent header only
  http_client_body   → match in HTTP request body
  http_header_names  → match in HTTP header names (not values)
  http.accept        → sticky buffer: HTTP Accept header value only
  ja3.hash           → TLS JA3 fingerprint hash
  → Using buffers avoids scanning entire packet = performance gain
  → Docs: https://suricata.readthedocs.io/en/latest/rules/http-keywords.html

[PCRE] — Perl Compatible Regular Expressions:
  pcre:"/regex/flags";
  → Flags: i=case-insensitive, R=relative to previous content match
  →        U=HTTP URI buffer, P=HTTP body buffer, C=HTTP cookie buffer
  → Negation: pcre:!"..." → trigger if regex does NOT match
  → WARNING: never base a rule solely on PCRE (too slow); pair with content:

  Example:
    pcre:"/^(?:login\/process|admin\/get|news)\.php$/RU";
    → Matches login/process.php, admin/get.php, or news.php in HTTP URI
    → R=relative to previous content match, U=HTTP URI buffer

[DSIZE] — payload size match:
  dsize:312;       → exact payload size (TCP segment, not total packet)
  dsize:>10000;    → payload larger than 10000 bytes
  → Useful for C2 beacon detection (fixed-size heartbeats)

[DETECTION_FILTER] — threshold after detection:
  detection_filter: track by_src, count 4, seconds 10;
  → Only alert if same detection fires ≥4 times within 10 seconds
  → by_src: group by source IP
  → by_dst: group by destination IP
  → Reduces noise for bursty traffic

[METADATA — required]:
  sid:10000001;    → signature ID, must be unique
  rev:1;           → revision number
  reference:url,link.to.source;

=== DETECTION APPROACHES ===
1. Signature-based: content patterns unique to known malware
2. Anomaly/behavior-based: dsize thresholds, beaconing intervals, unusual ports
3. Stateful protocol analysis: flow states, unexpected protocol transitions

=== RULE DEVELOPMENT TIPS ===
  → Always use flow:established,to_server for TCP HTTP rules
  → Use buffers (http_method, http_uri, etc.) instead of raw content when possible
  → Never write a rule that relies ONLY on PCRE
  → Add multiple content: checks before PCRE to pre-filter
  → Use nocase on known case-insensitive fields (URIs, User-Agents)
  → Use detection_filter to reduce false positives for volume-based alerts
  → Test with: sudo suricata -r file.pcap -l . -k none

examples.label: Minimal alert rule structure
examples.command: alert tcp $HOME_NET any -> $EXTERNAL_NET any (msg:"Test rule"; content:"pattern"; sid:1000001; rev:1;)

examples.label: HTTP method + URI buffer matching
examples.command: alert http any any -> any any (msg:"HTTP GET to /admin"; content:"GET"; http_method; content:"/admin"; http_uri; sid:1000002; rev:1;)

examples.label: Flow + content + nocase
examples.command: alert tcp any any -> any any (msg:"User-Agent Mozilla"; content:"User-Agent: Mozilla"; nocase; flow:established,to_server; sid:8001; rev:1;)

examples.label: Offset + depth (start/end window)
examples.command: alert tcp any any -> any any (msg:"Protocol command at offset 0"; content:"|01 02 03|"; offset:0; depth:5; sid:3003; rev:1;)

examples.label: Distance + within (relative chained window)
examples.command: alert http any any -> any any (msg:"GET /admin with gap"; content:"GET"; offset:0; depth:4; content:"/admin"; distance:10; within:80; sid:3001; rev:1;)

examples.label: PCRE on HTTP URI (relative, case-insensitive)
examples.command: alert http any any -> any any (msg:"PHP admin URI"; content:"/"; http_uri; pcre:"/^(?:login\/process|admin\/get)\.php$/RU"; sid:1000003; rev:1;)

examples.label: dsize exact match (C2 fixed-size beacon)
examples.command: alert tcp $HOME_NET any -> any any (msg:"C2 beacon size 312"; dsize:312; detection_filter: track by_src, count 3, seconds 10; sid:3000001; rev:1;)

examples.label: JA3 hash match (TLS fingerprint)
examples.command: alert tls any any -> any any (msg:"Malware TLS"; ja3.hash; content:"473cd7cb9faa642487833865d516e578"; sid:1002; rev:1;)

examples.label: File extraction rule
examples.command: alert http any any -> any any (msg:"FILE store all"; filestore; sid:2; rev:1;)

recommended.note: Suricata config and ruleset management — needed before writing/deploying rules.
Real-world rule examples: PowerShell Empire, Covenant, Sliver, Dridex detection.
